subject: residential-tenancies-act-lqa
note: 4A, 4-5 October 2026, Claude (agent), for Legalese. Residential Tenancies Act 1987 (WA) 07-a0-00 and Residential Tenancies Regulations 1989 (WA) 05-ad0-00, for the scope in lqa.json. Every module is listed under the Part it encodes; the boundary modules (Part VI ss 82 and 85, the Interpretation Act modules) and the two case files are listed under each Part that uses them. wa-interpretation-act-1984.l4 is a byte-identical copy of subjects/au/wa/_jurisdiction/library/wa-interpretation-act-1984.l4 (l4 imports only from its own folder); wa-interpretation-act-extra.l4 encodes Interpretation Act ss 5, 16(2), 37(1)(b) and 74, which decide forks FK-04, FK-21 and FK-26. The console scheme is not drafted at 4A in this run: another agent drafts it from the L4. The schema requires scheme to be an object naming a file and an id, so it names the file and id the scheme is to have (scheme.js, residential-tenancies-act-lqa); until that file exists the checker reports that the scheme does not load. See ENCODING-NOTES.md.

provisions: s 3 'lessor' (as the lessor under an agreement, including a successor or assignee: FK-13)
s 3 'pet' (whether an animal is an assistance animal is a fact)
s 3 'tenant' (as the tenant or co-tenants under an agreement)
Interpretation Act 1984 ss 61(1)(a)-(h), (2) and 62, through the jurisdiction library module, for every count of days and months
s 26B(4) (the court's power; whether it is satisfied, and what it orders, are facts)
s 29(1)(b), (2), (3) (so far as the bond turns on rent)
s 60(1)(a)-(i) (as circumstances with the day each happens), s 60(2)
s 30 as in force before 29 July 2024 (from 1 July 2013; with r 5CA), which s 99(3) continues

not_encoded.reason: Used by in-scope provisions only as facts: whether a form is approved (REF-01), which court is competent (REF-02), whether an animal is an assistance animal (REF-06), whether a person is a property manager (REF-10); 'prescribed' is encoded through each regulation (REF-07).

not_encoded.provisions: s 3 'bond administrator', 'Department', 'party' para (b), and the other s 3 terms
not_encoded.reason: Not used by an in-scope provision, or used only in bond lodgement (REF-08, REF-09).

not_encoded.provisions: s 26B(4) (what order the court makes); s 64(4)(b); s 65(2) (whether the court is satisfied); s 76C(3)
not_encoded.reason: Court discretion: whether the court is satisfied, and what it orders or modifies, are facts (REF-21, REF-54, REF-76). The encoding states when the power exists.
Out of scope (lqa.json): a single bond, instalments, receipt, lodgement and payment to the bond administrator do not turn on rent (REF-32 to REF-34, REF-46).
Whether rent is excessive, the matters the court regards, its order and any variation are the court's evaluation; the order's amount and period are inputs to s 32(5) and (7), which are encoded.

Termination of a tenant's interest on grounds of family violence (ss 71AB, 71AD, 71AE) is out of scope (REF-57 to REF-59); s 60(2), which says such a termination does not end the agreement for other tenants, is encoded.

Out of scope (lqa.json). Where an in-scope provision reads them they enter as facts: a notice of termination under the Act, its form (s 61, r 18, Form 1C), a court order and the day it operates, abandonment (REF-53 to REF-65, REF-69, REF-70, REF-74).

not_encoded.provisions: s 30 as in force before 1 July 2013; s 31A as in force before 29 July 2024
not_encoded.reason: No in-scope outcome turns on them except through r 5CA (encoded) and as history: a past change under the former s 31A counts for s 31A(2)(b)(ii) by Interpretation Act s 16(2) (encoded), and s 100(3) applies the present s 31A to agreements in force on 29 July 2024.

not_encoded.provisions: Regulations other than rr 5B, 5CA, 5CB, 7D, 7F, 7FA, 10AD, 10A, 11, 12I; r 18 and Schedule 4 Form 1C
not_encoded.reason: Out of scope (lqa.json); the prescribed form for s 61 is a fact (REF-64). rr 7C and 7E are spent (REF-92).

not_encoded.provisions: Interpretation Act 1984 ss 71 and 72 (in the jurisdiction library module)
not_encoded.reason: Held in the byte-identical copy of the library module but read by no in-scope rule: the offence provisions' penalties are out of scope (REF-50).

not_encoded.provisions: The general law of service by actual receipt (s 85(1) being permissive)
not_encoded.reason: Not in the Act; fork FK-12 records that an in-scope notice sent by email is not given under s 85, and the encoding gives it no day of giving.
